001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
004import java.util.ArrayList;
005import java.util.List;
006import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
007import java.util.concurrent.atomic.LongAdder;
008
009/**
010 * Metrics are cheap, numeric counters about the logging system itself - for example how
011 * many events an appender has dropped, or how often a reused encoder buffer had to shrink
012 * itself back down. Unlike {@link LogAlerts}, which records discrete events (each with a
013 * message/throwable, kept in a bounded ring buffer), metrics are just running totals: no
014 * per-call allocation, no ring buffer entry, no listener dispatch.
015 * <p>
016 * An instance is available from every {@link LogConfig#metrics()}. Components that are
017 * {@linkplain LogProvider provided} config, or that are
018 * {@linkplain LogLifecycle#start( LogConfig) started} with config, should prefer
019 * capturing {@code config.metrics()} over reaching for global state.
020 * <p>
021 * Deliberately a separate type from {@link LogAlerts} rather than more methods on it -
022 * the two are meant to be independently replaceable (e.g. a future Micrometer-backed
023 * {@code LogMetrics} without needing to also replace how alerts are recorded).
024 *
025 * @see LogConfig#metrics()
026 */
027public sealed interface LogMetrics permits DefaultLogMetrics {
028
029        /**
030         * Counter name for the global count of log events dropped without ever being written
031         * anywhere - for example an appender dropping events on reentry. Incremented whenever
032         * a drop happens regardless of whether that particular drop is also logged/alerted,
033         * since counting and alerting/logging are separate concerns.
034         */
035        static final String EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC = "events.dropped";
036
037        /**
038         * Counter name for the global count of times a reused encoder buffer had its backing
039         * storage shrunk back down after growing past its configured max size (see
040         * {@link LogEncoder.Buffer#isOversized()}). An occasional trim is normal and expected
041         * once in a while, but resizing <em>often</em> is a sign the configured max size (or
042         * the initial size) doesn't match the actual event sizes being logged - worth
043         * watching, not erroring on, hence {@link #warnCounter(String, long)} rather than
044         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}.
045         */
046        static final String BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC = "buffer.trimmed";
047
048        /**
049         * Counter name for the global count of log events an appender failed to write - the
050         * encoder or output threw while appending, so the event was caught, alerted (see
051         * {@link LogAlerts#error(Class, String, Throwable)}), and lost rather than retried.
052         * Kept separate from {@link #EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC}: a drop is a deliberate skip (the
053         * appender chose not to write), while this is an unexpected failure partway through
054         * actually trying to - different root causes worth distinguishing when triaging.
055         */
056        static final String EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC = "events.failed";
057
058        /**
059         * Increments a counter for something worth tracking as "this happens and it matters".
060         * @param name counter name, e.g. {@link #EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC} or a logger name.
061         * @param increment amount to add, usually {@code 1}.
062         */
063        public void errorCounter(String name, long increment);
064
065        /**
066         * Like {@link #errorCounter(String, long)} but for something worth tracking yet less
067         * significant than an error - a trend worth watching rather than something that, by
068         * itself, indicates a problem. Kept as a separate counter namespace from
069         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}: the same {@code name} passed to both is two
070         * distinct counters, not one shared one.
071         * @param name counter name, e.g. {@link #BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC}.
072         * @param increment amount to add, usually {@code 1}.
073         */
074        public void warnCounter(String name, long increment);
075
076        /**
077         * A snapshot of every counter recorded via {@link #errorCounter(String, long)} and
078         * {@link #warnCounter(String, long)}. Counters are monotonically increasing for the
079         * life of the process, like a Prometheus/Micrometer counter - there is no reset
080         * method; a downstream metrics system computes rate of change rather than relying on
081         * the counter itself being reset.
082         * @return immutable snapshot.
083         */
084        public List<Counter> counters();
085
086        /**
087         * A single named counter's current value, as returned by {@link #counters()}.
088         *
089         * @param name counter name, as passed to a counter method like
090         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}.
091         * @param level how much this counter matters - not a log level routing decision, just
092         * a signal of significance, mirroring the counter method it came from (e.g.
093         * {@link Level#ERROR} for {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}, {@link Level#WARNING}
094         * for {@link #warnCounter(String, long)}).
095         * @param count current value.
096         */
097        record Counter(String name, Level level, long count) {
098        }
099
100        /**
101         * The fixed, well known set of counters RainbowGum itself records - as opposed to the
102         * open ended, per logger name counters {@link LogAlerts#error(LogEvent)} also drives
103         * into {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}. Enumerable on purpose: consumers that
104         * want to bind every well known counter to something else (a Micrometer
105         * {@code FunctionCounter} per constant, for example) can loop over {@link #values()}
106         * instead of hand listing each {@code String}/{@link Level} pair themselves.
107         */
108        enum StandardMetric {
109
110                /**
111                 * See {@link #EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC}.
112                 */
113                EVENTS_DROPPED(EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC, Level.ERROR),
114                /**
115                 * See {@link #BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC}.
116                 */
117                BUFFER_TRIMMED(BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC, Level.WARNING),
118                /**
119                 * See {@link #EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC}.
120                 */
121                EVENTS_FAILED(EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC, Level.ERROR);
122
123                private final String metricName;
124
125                private final Level level;
126
127                StandardMetric(String metricName, Level level) {
128                        this.metricName = metricName;
129                        this.level = level;
130                }
131
132                /**
133                 * The counter name, as passed to {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}/
134                 * {@link #warnCounter(String, long)} and matched against {@link Counter#name()}.
135                 * @return counter name.
136                 */
137                public String metricName() {
138                        return metricName;
139                }
140
141                /**
142                 * Which counter method this metric is recorded through - {@link Level#ERROR} for
143                 * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}, {@link Level#WARNING} for
144                 * {@link #warnCounter(String, long)} - and so also which {@link Counter#level()}
145                 * it shows up under in {@link #counters()}.
146                 * @return level.
147                 */
148                public Level level() {
149                        return level;
150                }
151
152        }
153
154}
155
156final class DefaultLogMetrics implements LogMetrics {
157
158        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> errorCounters = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
159
160        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> warnCounters = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
161
162        @Override
163        public void errorCounter(String name, long increment) {
164                errorCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()).add(increment);
165        }
166
167        @Override
168        public void warnCounter(String name, long increment) {
169                warnCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()).add(increment);
170        }
171
172        @Override
173        public List<Counter> counters() {
174                List<Counter> list = new ArrayList<>(errorCounters.size() + warnCounters.size());
175                for (var e : errorCounters.entrySet()) {
176                        list.add(new Counter(e.getKey(), Level.ERROR, e.getValue().sum()));
177                }
178                for (var e : warnCounters.entrySet()) {
179                        list.add(new Counter(e.getKey(), Level.WARNING, e.getValue().sum()));
180                }
181                return List.copyOf(list);
182        }
183
184}
